join_order.notes: Scan keyword/keyword.{off,dat}; read keyword/id.bin at match. ~134k rows, single pass.

country_code is dict-encoded int16; resolve '[us]' dict id via country_code.dict.{off,dat}, then scan country_code.bin (int16[Ncn]) and collect company_name.id where == us_dict_id. Use std::unordered_set<int32_t> sized ~10k, or a bitset(max_company_id+1) since max_company_id <= 234997 (~30KB bitset). Prefer bitset for O(1) lookup.

join_order.build: movie_keyword aux CSR bucket for kw_id
join_order.notes: Use indexes/movie_keyword__keyword_id__{offsets,rowids}.bin. Range [off[kw_id], off[kw_id+1]) gives 41,840 mk rows; read movie_keyword/movie_id.bin at each rowid. Dedupe is essentially a no-op (~99.95% unique); collecting into a std::vector<int32_t> is fine.

join_order.probe: movie_companies via primary CSR on movie_id
join_order.notes: For each candidate movie_id, use indexes/movie_companies__movie_id__offsets.bin to get [lo,hi). Scan movie_companies/company_id.bin[lo..hi) and short-circuit if any company_id is in us_company_set. Output: ~4,377 surviving movie_ids.

join_order.probe: cast_info via primary CSR on movie_id
join_order.notes: For each surviving movie_id, use indexes/cast_info__movie_id__offsets.bin to read [lo,hi) of cast_info/person_id.bin. Total ~258,755 person_ids produced.
Use indexes/name__id__pos.bin (int32[max_id+2]). For each person_id pid: row = pos[pid]; if row >= 0, read name/name.{off,dat} at row and update running MIN.

filters.notes: Single dimension row resolves to kw_id (observed: 117).
Dict-encoded int16 column; resolve dict id once, then linear scan.
Bitset on company_id makes this O(rows_in_movie) with cheap probes.

data_structures.us_company_set: bitset(max_company_id+1) ≈ 30 KB (preferred over hash_set for cache locality and zero allocation churn)
data_structures.surviving_movie_ids: std::vector<int32_t> reserve(5000) (optional intermediate; can fuse step 4 into step 5)
data_structures.aggregation: single scalar: std::string_view running_min (initially empty/unset); lexicographic compare on each lookup

parallelism.threads: auto(nproc) — but workload is small (~4.4k surviving movies, ~260k name lookups). Recommend single-threaded execution to avoid synchronization overhead; if parallelized, partition candidate_movie_ids across threads and reduce per-thread running mins at the end.

person_id -> name row position for MIN(name)

fusion_notes: Fuse step 4 and step 5: for each candidate movie_id, do the US-company short-circuit check, and on success immediately probe cast_info and update MIN inline (no intermediate surviving_movie_ids vector needed).

Reading name.name varlen is the costliest per-row operation; running MIN compare is cheap (varlen string_view lex compare). No early-exit possible since MIN over unsorted lex strings can be improved by any later row.
